auto.text: The team lists the Autonomous Award at its UVM event.
In one Pine Tree final it reached the line just after 747 and got much less fuel; in one New England final it stuck on fuel and its alliance lost auto.

cycle.text: A poster at Pine Tree saw it feed by reversing its intake and hopper rollers instead of shooting over.
In one New England final it collected in front of the opponents' hub to stop short cycles, then crossed the bump past a defender and emptied its hopper.
In a Burns division match, a partner herded fuel and counter-defended for it.

gave_up.text: It had many power consumption issues in the season; its logs looked as good as other teams', and it guesses at a battery or connector difference.
It had autos that it never ran, and "some shoot" that it never used in a match.
The urethane drum coating was a real pain that the team would not recommend.
A host says its net slowed it at the trench.

changed.text: One poster calls it a rebuild from week 0; another says the team brought both robots and drove this one in some matches.
Floor rollers became belts between the URI and UVM events, and the intake went from rack and pinion to a capstan after teeth were damaged at URI.
Another team helped diagnose its power draw at UVM.

outcome.text: 62-12-1 in official play; won the New England District Championship; did not play in a championship division.

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Take fuel fast with little current, and survive hard impacts

functions.type: roller intake deployed by a capstan

facts.text: Two 2 in top rollers driven by two X44s
A 1.25 in bottom kicker driven by the X44 that drives the floor
Compression between top and lower rollers, about
The lower the compression the less the motor bogged down, so the team used the least that still worked
Capstan: the middle of a rope is fixed to the hub and its ends to the front and back of the intake; turning the hub pulls one side in and pays out the other
Since the change only rope tension needed adjusting
The capstan was not prototyped, since the team had used some form of it for three years; the roller positions were prototyped through several iterations

cost.text: The earlier rack sheared teeth whenever the intake took a hard impact

solves.text: Feed fuel without balls spinning in place

facts.text: Drew less current and gave somewhat more balls per second than rollers, after several iterations of both
After the change both auto-shot timers had to be shortened by over half a second
Gaps between belts make natural lanes, so volleys three to four balls wide came more consistently
It shoots the same distance regardless of how fast or how many balls enter
Aluminum tube 6 in in diameter and 1/8 in thick, with four layers of PMC-780 urethane, turned down and balanced with bolts in the side plates
Moment of inertia, a little over
The kicker roller that feeds it turned out not to be really needed
The hood covers about 24 degrees, of which about 12 are used

cost.text: The urethane coating was a real pain; the team would not recommend it if there are other options

solves.text: Extrapolate and interpolate drivetrain, flywheel and hood states

facts.text: Average loop time
Odometry thread
Interpolating maps of hood and flywheel with drivetrain velocity compensation, for shoot on the move; the same post says it had "some shoot" never used in a match
A battery and energy logger
Frame 30 in wide and 24 in long
A host calls it so heavy with fuel that a defender had to sit a bit forward on the bump to stop it

decisions.because: hard impacts sheared the teeth of the rack
it drew less current, gave more balls per second and stopped balls spinning in place
more compression bogged down the motor
looking back, the team says performance, units libraries and strict compile-time checks likely made this its most reliable software season
